s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cutaneous lesion with purpuric patches, ulceration, and bleeding
salient_findings: Enlarging purpuric patch on the left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
Multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
key_facts: Lesion first developed in March 2014
Rapid growth and extension occurred in June 2014
Lesion involves left anterior scalp, left parietal scalp, left forehead, and left lateral cheek
No evidence of lymphadenopathy
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31
Cells were negative for CK5
Strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors
Ki-67 proliferation marker analysis was performed
Chest and abdominal CT scan showed no evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases

shortlist.label: Cutaneous angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a rapidly growing, ulcerated purpuric lesion with histopathological features of irregular slitlike spaces and CD31 positivity

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to cutaneous angiosarcoma, with overlapping clinical and histopathological features, but less specific to the skin

shortlist.label: Kaposi sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with purpuric patches and can have a similar histopathological appearance, but typically has a more multifocal distribution and association with immunosuppression

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause purpuric lesions, but typically has a more inflammatory histopathological appearance and lacks the characteristic slitlike spaces

shortlist.label: Pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a rapidly growing lesion, but typically has a more benign clinical course and distinct histopathological features

raw.rationale: The presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes in the dermis, cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei, and strong immunopositivity for CD31 and ADRB receptors, along with rapid growth and extension of the lesion, are characteristic features of cutaneous angiosarcoma.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as cutaneous angiosarcoma is a more specific diagnosis that matches the clinical presentation and histopathological findings.

rejected.label: Kaposi sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically associated with human herpesvirus 8 infection and has distinct histopathological features, such as spindle cell proliferation and hyaline globules, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: Characterized by inflammation of small vessels and would not typically present with the same degree of rapid growth and extension as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Pyogenic granuloma
rejected.why: Usually presents as a solitary, rapidly growing lesion, but histopathologically is characterized by a mixture of granulation tissue and inflammatory cells, which does not match the description provided.
